entries.back_en: "What... What do you do in this place?"
entries.note: Archaic 'be ye doing' rendered well with 'fazeis vós'.

entries.back_en: "It's really true—and not just any dragon, no! They say it's the legendary Dragon of Doom, which will bring ruin to the Empire!"
"And... What is your intent with this dragon?"
"You believe you can do such a thing? You are but an insignificant mortal."
entries.note: Source 'mortals' is plural; target uses singular 'mortal'.

entries.back_en: "You do not understand the power of that which you would destroy. This is a dragon."

"A dragon is a force of nature in itself. You may as well seek to fight a volcano or the very earth itself! Dragons give birth to your kind, grant life, and truly take it away. They are to you as you are to an insect. In your terms..."
entries.note: Word order slightly reordered but meaning preserved.

entries.back_en: "... Would you dare fight a god?"
"'It is as I supposed... It is not the nature of mortals to change their ways..."
entries.note: Stray leading apostrophe before 'É' carried over from source formatting; meaning fine.

entries.back_en: "They say a dragon or something is supposed to appear tonight... So we were ordered to watch this area."
